summary: The virtio console as a program sees it: with one of its ports as the kernel's console, as on every guest case's machine, and its absence when the boot line names the UART, each case booting the test image and running hvcmusl; and as the kernel stops it: the device reset at a restart, and a panic's record that reaches the port with the transmit lock held; and as QEMU adds and removes ports after the boot: a console port that becomes hvc0, gets the console's record through emerg_wr and is a terminal of its own, and a generic port that is a byte device by its number and its name

cases.behavior: A guest case's machine has a virtio console and no UART, and the kernel takes the device's port 1 as its console by the console=vport0p1 that etude adds to the boot line: the device is bound to virtio_console, /dev/vport0p1 is the console terminal, and the log names the port

assertions.checks: /proc/cmdline has the word console=vport0p1.
One device of /sys/bus/virtio has DRIVER=virtio_console in its uevent.
/dev/vport0p1 is the character device 245:1, and /dev/hvc0, a console port's node, does not exist.
/dev lists vport0p1 once and hvc0 never.
An open of /dev/vport0p1 is a terminal with the modes and the size of /dev/console.
The kernel's log has the driver's record of its binding and the console's record of the port, console: enabled: vport0p1, port 1 of the device.

native.reason: the port is a device of QEMU's, which etude gives a guest case's machine, and the Lenovo has no virtio console

cases.behavior: A guest case whose boot options name a console keeps the UART, and its machine has no virtio console: with console=ttyS0 neither /dev/vport0p1 nor /dev/hvc0 exists, no device is bound to virtio_console, and the log names no port as the console

assertions.checks: /proc/cmdline has the word console=ttyS0 and no console=vport0p1.
/dev/vport0p1 and /dev/hvc0 do not exist, by name or in /dev's listing; no device of /sys/bus/virtio is bound to virtio_console; and the log has no record of a port as the console.

native.reason: the case is the other half of guest.hvc.port, a machine of QEMU's without the virtio console; the Lenovo's UART is the console of every native run

cases.behavior: a restart from the debug shell of a machine whose log goes to a virtio console's port beside COM1 has the driver give the console back to COM1 and reset the device before the kernel restarts the machine

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes its evidence, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot to the debug shell with the log on the virtio console's port 0 and COM1, run reboot and wait for the machine to end

assertions.checks: the boot gives the log to the virtconsole, console: enabled: hvc0, port 0 of virtio0, for output alone, since COM1 is named after it

after reboot is typed the console leaves the port, console: disabled: hvc0: the system stops, and then the driver says virtio_console: shutdown: virtio0: reset, which it says only when virtio_halt's reset of the device ended
the kernel says reboot: restarting after that record, so the device is reset before the processors stop
the machine ends by QEMU's SHUTDOWN event with the reason guest-reset

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the console's device is QEMU's virtio-serial-pci, which the Lenovo does not have, and the machine ends by a reset

cases.behavior: a panic with the virtio console's transmit lock held, as a processor the panic stops would hold it, on a machine whose only console is the device's virtserialport, still gives the host the panic's record through that port

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes its evidence, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the test image with rach2.vconpanic on a machine whose console is the virtio port, read the panic's record from the port, and end the machine

assertions.checks: the port carries the console, console: enabled: vport0p1, port 1 of the device
the panic's record, panic: stopped: virtio_console: panic test: the transmit side is held, reaches the host through the port, which is a virtserialport and so not reached by emerg_wr

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case panics the kernel on purpose on a virtio console of QEMU's, which the Lenovo does not have

cases.behavior: a virtio console of six ports that a machine with COM1 has from the boot, with a generic port named org.rach2.boot, gives every port its nodes: the generic port is /dev/vport0p1 and /dev/virtio-ports/org.rach2.boot, a byte device that tells the host's end it is open; a console port added through QMP after the boot becomes hvc0, which the boot line names, gets the console's record of it through emerg_wr and is /dev/hvc0, a terminal of its own whose output reaches the host; and a port added at port 3 through QMP is /dev/vport0p3 and /dev/virtio-ports/org.rach2.late, which reads and writes the host's end and goes when QMP removes the port; and two ports added at ports 4 and 5 through QMP, whose names are 255 bytes long and differ only in their last byte, are listed whole in /dev/virtio-ports and open by the listed names, through paths of 273 bytes

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes its evidence, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot to the debug shell, run hvcmusl's boot mode, add a virtconsole with a file as its host's end and run hvcmusl's tty mode, add a virtserialport at port 3 whose host's end is an abstract Unix socket, which the scenario connects to and writes pong to, and run hvcmusl's late mode, remove the port and run hvcmusl's gone mode, add two virtserialports at ports 4 and 5 with names of 255 bytes and run hvcmusl's long mode, and end the machine

assertions.checks: hvcmusl boot exits 0: one device is bound to virtio_console; /dev/vport0p1 and /dev/virtio-ports/org.rach2.boot are one character device of major 245; with no host's end a read gives the end of a file, poll gives POLLHUP and not POLLOUT, a write without a wait fails with EAGAIN and a second open fails with EBUSY; /dev/hvc0 is absent; and the log says console: none: console=hvc0 names no port now

the virtconsole's host's end gets the driver's record virtio_console: port: virtio0: port 0 added, which the kernel writes before the port carries the log, so only through emerg_wr, whose bytes QEMU gives its console port 0

hvcmusl tty exits 0: /dev/hvc0 comes while hvcmusl sleeps and so lets the driver's thread run, which the debug shell does not; it is the terminal 229:0, which takes a line, and /dev/vport0p0, the console port's vport node, refuses an open with ENXIO
the line written to /dev/hvc0 reaches the virtconsole's host's end as hvc-tty and a carriage return and newline, through the terminal's discipline

hvcmusl late exits 0: /dev/virtio-ports/org.rach2.late comes; /dev/vport0p3 and /dev/virtio-ports/org.rach2.late are one character device of major 245, which takes a line, gives pong and a newline, the bytes of its host's end, and polls writable
the line written to the late port reaches its host's end as ping and a newline
after QMP's device_del, hvcmusl gone exits 0: the late port's nodes go and the boot port's stays

after QMP's device_add of two ports at 4 and 5 named org.rach2. and 244 bytes of n and then a or b, hvcmusl long exits 0: /dev/virtio-ports lists each name once and whole, and each name getdents64 gives opens /dev/virtio-ports/NAME as the device of /dev/vport0p4 or /dev/vport0p5

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the ports are QEMU's virtio-serial-pci's, added and removed through QMP, which the Lenovo has neither of
